teacher.bio:
Thanh has more than 15 years of marketing experience. He spent eight years in B2C retail and led marketing teams at Co.opmart supermarkets. He then worked in B2B marketing for six years, focusing on branding, communications, marketing plans, international events and trade shows.

Working in both settings shaped an approach to marketing grounded in operations, customer behavior and business decisions.

experience.detail: Led marketing teams at Co.opmart supermarkets.
Focused on branding, corporate communications, marketing plans, international events and trade shows.

teacher.research:
Bachelor’s degree in Marketing.
MSc in Marketing.
Doctoral studies in Economics and Management at Tomas Bata University in Zlín, Czech Republic.
teacher.positioning: Connecting marketing practice with research and teaching.
teacher.teaching: Alongside his marketing work, Thanh teaches and speaks as a guest lecturer at colleges and universities.
teacher.perspective: I built this learning portal to share what I’ve learned through work, research and teaching. I select and organize the material so it’s easy to follow, grounded in research and connected to real situations. I hope the resources and conversations here help learners broaden their perspective, think independently and apply what they learn with confidence.

advanced-communication.title: Advanced Communication Skills
advanced-communication.description: Practice purposeful communication in study and work. Use realistic scenarios to develop listening, questioning, clear expression, feedback and skills for difficult conversations.

lectureAccess.title: Lectures for enrolled learners
lectureAccess.message: Only learners enrolled in the course can view lecture content. Contact the lecturer for access.

advanced-communication.subtitle: Listen to understand, speak to connect and work through problems together.
advanced-communication.method: Blended instruction with an emphasis on practice
advanced-communication.audienceLabel: For students and working professionals across disciplines

syllabus.overview: Learn to communicate with a clear purpose and adapt to the situation. Explore what affects a conversation and practice listening, confirming information, asking questions, structuring a message, giving feedback and handling disagreement. The course introduces enough theory to explain why an approach works in one situation and may be less effective in another. Most of the time is spent on pair and small-group practice, case analysis and feedback. The course is designed for 20 to 30 learners and runs for eight 45-minute periods over two in-person sessions.
objectives: Analyze the purpose, participants, context and possible sources of misunderstanding in a conversation.
Listen actively, ask questions, summarize and confirm information.
Express a clear, focused message that suits the audience and channel.
Give constructive feedback and handle disagreements respectfully, keeping the discussion focused on the issue.
Assess your communication habits and identify what to practice next.
outcomes: Prepare for a conversation with a clear purpose and expected outcome.
Ask questions and confirm information to reduce misunderstandings.
Express an opinion coherently and adjust your wording to the situation.
Give and receive feedback grounded in specific events, behaviors and impacts.
Complete a communication role-play and explain the choices you made.

sessions.title: Giving and receiving constructive feedback
sessions.focus: Describe the situation, observable behavior and impact. Practice giving feedback, asking follow-up questions and agreeing on changes.
sessions.output: An evidence-based feedback exchange and an appropriate response.

sessions.title: Managing disagreement and difficult conversations
sessions.focus: Notice tension, stay focused on the issue, clarify concerns and find a practical next step.
sessions.output: A difficult-conversation script and an agreement on what to do next.

sessions.title: Email, messages and meetings
sessions.focus: Choose the right channel, make a clear request, confirm decisions and record follow-up actions.
sessions.output: An edited work email or message and a meeting follow-up template.

sessions.title: Integrated practice and final assessment
sessions.focus: Combine listening, questioning, clear expression, feedback and disagreement management in one scenario. Complete the final assessment.
sessions.output: A role-play, observation form and individual practice plan.

Progress from guided practice to scenarios with fewer hints. Assess your own work and choose one behavior to practice further.

teamwork.title: Teamwork Skills
teamwork.description: Learn to coordinate work as a team. Practice agreeing on goals, assigning responsibilities, planning, tracking progress, making decisions and resolving disagreements through practical tasks.

lectureAccess.title: Lectures for enrolled learners
lectureAccess.message: Only learners enrolled in the course can view lecture content. Contact the lecturer for access.

teamwork.subtitle: Agree on the goal, clarify responsibilities and coordinate the work.
teamwork.audienceLabel: For students and working professionals across disciplines

syllabus.overview: Learn to coordinate work toward a shared goal. Explore what makes teams effective and practice setting objectives, defining roles, assigning responsibilities, planning, tracking progress, running meetings, making decisions and handling disagreement. The course introduces group processes and individual accountability, with most of the time spent on collaborative tasks, simulations and feedback. It is designed for 20 to 30 learners working in groups of four to five, with eight 45-minute periods over two in-person sessions.
objectives: Explain the main factors that influence team effectiveness.
Set a shared goal, define the scope and agree on how to work together.
Assign roles and responsibilities and plan how to track progress.
Participate in meetings, share information, make decisions and manage disagreement.
Evaluate the team’s results and your contribution to identify areas for improvement.
outcomes: Define the goal and deliverable for a team task.
Create a work plan that shows who is responsible, the deadlines and the expected outputs.
Use a tool to track progress and record decisions.
Help resolve problems and disagreements using evidence, criteria and shared goals.
Complete a team task and review how the team worked.

effective-learning-entrepreneurship.title: Effective Learning and Innovative Entrepreneurship
effective-learning-entrepreneurship.description: Practice independent learning, time management and focus. Then work with a team to investigate a real problem, build a prototype and revise your idea based on feedback.

lectureAccess.title: Lectures for enrolled learners
lectureAccess.message: Only learners enrolled in the course can view lecture content. Contact the lecturer for access.

effective-learning-entrepreneurship.subtitle: Find a study routine that works for you and try solving a problem in your field.

syllabus.overview:
In the first session, you’ll try ways to study and review material independently, then choose an approach that fits your schedule. In the second session, you’ll work with a team to investigate a problem in your field, build a prototype and revise it after receiving feedback.\
\
The course consists of eight 45-minute periods over two sessions. Each session includes 180 minutes of instruction, excluding breaks. Classes have 20 to 30 learners, working in teams of four to six.\
\
The classroom test helps your team decide what to revise and investigate next. To see whether the solution meets a real need, test it further with the people who would use it. After the course, you can use your personal plan to track and maintain the study routine you chose.
objectives: Set your own learning goals, monitor progress and adjust how you study.
Choose evidence-based study methods and verify information when using AI.
Identify a workplace problem, assess the resources available and test a way to address it.
outcomes: Create a study plan with milestones at 30, 60 and 90 days, including deliverables and how you’ll track them.
Recall material from memory, check it against the source, correct errors and schedule review.
Describe a problem and distinguish observations from assumptions.
Write a value proposition, build a prototype and plan a test of one assumption.
Explain what the available evidence shows and decide what to revise next.

sessions.title: Taking charge of your learning
sessions.focus: Distinguish learning to remember, learning to do and learning to create value. Review how you study and choose one thing to improve.
sessions.output: A baseline self-assessment and one priority goal.

sessions.title: Setting goals and staying focused
sessions.focus: Choose a deliverable, make a realistic schedule and plan for distractions or schedule changes.
sessions.output: A plan with 30-, 60- and 90-day milestones and a weekly study schedule.

sessions.title: Retrieval practice and spaced review
sessions.focus: Recall material without looking, then check and correct your answers. Schedule review and choose methods that fit the task.
sessions.output: A corrected self-test and revised review schedule.

sessions.title: Adjusting your study routine and using AI
sessions.focus: Plan, try and record what you would change. Use AI to suggest questions and verify answers against sources, or do the exercise without AI.
sessions.output: A verification log and a plan to repeat the task independently.

sessions.title: Entrepreneurial thinking and value creation
sessions.focus: Compare starting a business with improving work inside an organization. Look for opportunities to use technology, reduce waste or meet a community need.
sessions.output: Three identified problems and one opportunity the team chooses to explore.

sessions.title: Learning from users
sessions.focus: Ask users about something they have done. Use real data or a simulation to distinguish evidence from assumptions.
sessions.output: A problem statement and interview notes that identify their sources.

sessions.title: Prototyping and testing a solution
sessions.focus: Explain the benefit to users, identify resources and build a simple prototype. Agree on criteria before testing one assumption.
sessions.output: A prototype and a record of the first test.

sessions.title: Presenting results and planning next steps
sessions.focus: Present your observations and revisions. Review your contribution, complete the final assessment and decide what to test next.
sessions.output: A mini-project, individual plan and final assessment.

teachingApproach: Each period starts with a short explanation and an example. Then you try the task, receive feedback and revise in class.
Choose a situation from your field, such as a technical trade, service, arts and culture or community work.
If you meet users between sessions, ask permission before recording information. For simulations, identify your source and plan a follow-up test with actual users.
You can work on paper. AI is optional.

assessment.name: Practical exercises
assessment.description: Four exercises worth five points each: set a goal, recall material and correct errors, analyze a problem, and prepare interview questions.

assessment.name: Mini-project
assessment.description: The team deliverable is worth up to 40 points under the rubric. Each person’s explanation and contribution are worth up to 10 points.

assessment.name: Individual plan and reflection
assessment.description: Each piece is worth five points. Cover goals, schedule, study methods, how you’ll track and adjust your plan, and reflection on how you learn.

assessment.name: Participation and contribution
assessment.description: Up to three points for preparation, four for cooperation and three for specific feedback. You may respond in writing.

tracks.title: Improving a Workshop Task
tracks.subtitle: Reduce tool mix-ups or clarify instructions in a training workshop.
tracks.task: Observe how tools are collected and returned. Pick one cause you can check.
tracks.workflow: Ask regular tool users, sketch a different layout and test it under safe conditions.
tracks.product: A problem statement, prototype layout and notes on what to revise.
tracks.tools: Use the observation, interview and test templates under Learner Support.

tracks.title: Organizing Creative Activities
tracks.subtitle: Improve rehearsal, props preparation or the audience experience.
tracks.task: Identify a problem and talk to someone who experiences it directly.
tracks.workflow: Try a different way to share schedules, label props or guide the audience. Revise it after feedback.
tracks.product: A problem statement, prototype and notes on what you learned from feedback.
tracks.tools: Use the observation, interview and test templates under Learner Support.

tracks.title: Improving an Everyday Service
tracks.subtitle: Reduce waiting time, help people find information or reduce waste.
tracks.task: Observe one use of the service and choose an assumption to test.
tracks.workflow: Talk to users, build a simple prototype such as a sign, and watch them try it.
tracks.product: A problem statement, prototype and proposal for the next test.
tracks.tools: Use the observation, interview and test templates under Learner Support.

references.description: Reviews how retrieval practice and spaced review make learning more effective. Access to the article may be restricted.

references.title: Retrieval Practice Guide
references.description: Test yourself after studying, check your answers and correct errors.

references.title: Spaced Review Guide
references.description: Spread review across several sessions instead of doing it all at once.

references.description: A framework published in 2016 with 15 competencies across three areas.
Guidance for vocational institutions on organizing entrepreneurial learning activities.

references.title: Design Kit and Human-Centered Design Methods
references.description: Choose interviewing, prototyping and feedback methods that fit the project’s goals.

references.title: Guidance for Generative AI in Education and Research
references.description: Principles for responsible use in teaching and research, with learners and educators at the center.

support.title: Learning Skills Self-Assessment
support.description: Complete the form before the course to choose one habit to improve. Repeat after 14 days and review your work. The exercise at the end of session two shows what you can do so far. This classroom tool has not been validated as a measurement scale.
support.label: Available

support.title: 30-, 60- and 90-Day Learning Plan
support.description: Pick a skill relevant to your field and realistic for your schedule. For design, one 30-day goal could be to make an event poster independently, at the right size, with all the details and text readable on a phone.
support.label: Available

support.title: Effective Learning Methods Toolkit
support.description: After studying a short section, close the material and recall three key points, solve a problem or repeat a task. Reopen the material to find and fix errors. Familiarity when rereading can differ from what you can do independently. This review can be ungraded.
support.label: Available

support.title: Time Management and Focus Workbook
support.description: For two days, log study, paid work, travel, rest and social media. Find a regular time for study. Account for family responsibilities, equipment and your study space.
support.label: Available

support.title: Independent Learning and Verifying AI Output
support.description: Before asking AI, write down what you understand and where you’re stuck. Use AI to suggest questions, explain a point or review a draft, then check the output against your materials. Close the chat and try a similar task independently.
support.label: Available

support.title: Problem and Opportunity Worksheet
support.description: Observe a situation in your field and record what happened, when, who was affected and how. “Students need an app” already proposes a solution. Start with something you can check, such as newcomers missing rehearsals because notices are spread across group chats.
support.label: Available

support.title: User Interview Questions
support.description: Choose someone who has experienced the situation. Explain the purpose, ask permission and let them stop at any time. Record only what you need, use codes instead of names and ask separately before recording or taking photos. Assign an interviewer and a note-taker.
support.label: Available

support.title: Value Proposition and Idea Template
support.description: Describe your users, their task, your solution and what it improves over their current approach. A backstage team that wants fewer prop mix-ups might test a location chart before building an app.
support.label: Available

support.title: Guide to Prototyping and Testing a Solution
support.description: Decide what you want to learn before choosing a prototype such as a screen sketch, service script or paper model. Observe how users understand and use it. An MVP is the simplest version that can deliver value and support learning from real use. A poster can help test a message.
support.label: Available

support.title: Mini-project and Assessment Criteria
support.description: Teams of four to six choose a problem in their field, build a prototype and test one assumption. Submit a one-page analysis, evidence log, prototype and proposed revisions. Each person submits a 90-day learning plan and a short account of their contribution.
support.label: Available

support.title: Contact the Lecturer
support.description: Ask the lecturer about your learning plan or discuss issues that come up during the project.
support.label: Connect on Zalo
